text:
Support Bot: New customer question (FinchAI) via email -> “We want to enable quantization only for our background summarization endpoints, not for interactive chat. Is that possible? How do we scope it?”

Markus Klein: Yep this is exactly the route-scoped use case. They have 2 routes today: `chat_interactive` and `summarize_batch`.

Markus Klein: Can someone confirm the current guidance for doing it purely at the route config level (no per-request header hacks), and what the propagation time is?

Nikhil Sharma: For Hosted API beta: we support route-level enablement in Console + Config API. No request headers needed/encouraged.

Aditya Rao: +1. Positioning: keep chat on baseline, flip quant on the background route, start with a canary % if they’re nervous.

Markus Klein: Great. Do we have a crisp snippet we can send? They asked “how do we scope it”.

Elliot Price: Docs wording we’ve been using: “Quantization is enabled per Route. Each Route can pin a baseline model and optionally a quantization profile. Other Routes in the same org are unaffected.”

Elliot Price: I can paste a minimal example message + point them to Console steps.

Rafael Mendes: Operationally: if they enable it on `summarize_batch` only, rollback is also per-route toggle off. Changes should take effect quickly (order of minutes) once control plane pushes + runtime cache refresh.

Markus Klein: Cool. Any gotchas we should flag? They do background summaries so latency is less sensitive but they care about “format stability” (they output markdown + sometimes JSON).

Aditya Rao: Gotchas:
- If they rely on strict JSON mode/tool calling, advise canary + monitor parsing/validation errors.
- Use the “structured output” prompt set in their own evals if they have one.
- Start with int8 before int4 if they want conservative quality.

Nikhil Sharma: Also: quant profiles are model-specific + hardware scoped. So they can only enable it if the route’s model has a published profile in the library.

Markus Klein: Right. They’re on `rw-qwen2.5-72b` (I think). Is that in the first supported set?

Aditya Rao: For beta, yes, we have int8 and one int4 profile variant, but we’ve been recommending int8 for “format sensitive” workloads.

Elliot Price: Here’s a draft response you can send (feel free to edit):

Elliot Price: “Yes—quantization is scoped per API Route. You can enable it only on your background summarization route and keep interactive chat on baseline. In Console: Routes → select `summarize_batch` → Quantization → Enable → choose Profile (recommended: int8 to start) → optionally set Canary % (e.g., 10–25%) → Save. Leave `chat_interactive` quantization disabled. Rollback is immediate by toggling quantization off on that route. We recommend monitoring output-format validation errors (JSON parse failures, tool-calling schema failures) during the canary.”

Markus Klein: Nice. Can we add an API option too? They automate route config via CI.

Nikhil Sharma: We do have the config API. Keep it high level in support email (we don’t want to leak internal endpoint names). Something like: “You can also apply this via the Route Settings API/terraform, ask us for the exact payload.”

Rafael Mendes: +1. Also worth saying: if they have multiple customers/tenants under one org, scoping is by route not by end-user, so they should ensure the background route is truly separated.

Markus Klein: Good call.

Markus Klein: Sending to customer:
- confirm route-only enablement
- recommend int8 + canary
- mention rollback + monitoring
- offer to share config payload

Markus Klein: Will follow up if they want help splitting traffic between routes (some customers currently send both chat + summaries through one route).

Aditya Rao: If they’re mixing workloads on one route, the right answer is: create a dedicated summarization route + enable quant there. That’s the cleanest.

Elliot Price: Yep. Also remind them that the route-level audit log will show the change + who flipped it, which helps for enterprise change control.

Markus Klein: Sent. Will update thread when they respond.
